target_customer: Consumers and small businesses in US cities who wanted on demand errands and house cleaning booked from a phone
problem: Booking a trustworthy person for errands or a home clean meant phone tag with agencies or bidding on marketplaces.
business_model: On demand services marketplace with an hourly rate (25 dollars per hour at launch, later 38 dollars for cleaning per Wikipedia) and a share paid to contractors
product_category: On demand home services and errands

founders.name: Justin Kan
founders.background_notes: YC page bio says he founded Twitch, Exec and Justin.tv, later Atrium. Education not found.

founders.name: Amir Ghazvinian
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as Founder/CTO with no bio.

founders.name: Daniel Kan
founders.background_notes: YC page: built Exec (W12), Cruise (W14), now Fifth Door (F25). Wikipedia calls him Justin's brother.

exit.reason: Handybook bought Exec to expand on the West Coast; a TechCrunch headline put the price under 10 million dollars, not stated in the article text I read.

competitors.name: TaskRabbit
competitors.what: Marketplace where people post errands and tasks to be bid on

competitors.name: Zaarly
competitors.what: Real time marketplace for posted tasks, charging a 9.9 percent fee on electronic payments

technical_complexity.rationale: Mobile app with dispatch, messaging and payments; the hard part was operations and contractor supply, not technology.

defensibility.rationale: Flat hourly pricing and contractor pools were easy to copy, and by 2013 cleaning was over half of orders against many cleaning services and Handybook.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Handybook acquired Exec in Jan 2014; Exec had already shut its errand service in Sep 2013 to focus on cleaning.

market_need_then: Exec reported about 100 contractors and a couple thousand jobs by May 2012, over 11,000 contractor applicants in eight months by Mar 2013, and cleaning above 50 percent of orders.

branding.domain_note: Used iamexec.com rather than exec.com; it now redirects to handy.com.

identity.visual_style: A February 2013 redesign was covered by TechCrunch; details not recorded

branding.brand_signature: Calling contractors Execs, as in a personal executive assistant for anyone
branding.community_and_virality: Founder Justin Kan's profile drove launch press; Exec was nominated for a 2012 TechCrunchie award for fastest rising startup per Wikipedia.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong founder driven press and a nominated award, but a generic short word that fit errands better than cleaning and disappeared into Handy after the sale.

pivots.why: Cleaning was over 50 percent of orders
Shut errands to focus on cleaning

outcome_analysis: Exec raised a 3.3 million dollar seed in May 2012 from a YC family style group led by Sam Altman, found that cleaning dominated demand, spun off a cleaning app in Feb 2013 and closed errands in Sep 2013. Handybook then bought it in Jan 2014 for a reported figure under 10 million dollars. The result was a modest exit that gave the investors a return, driven by a focused pivot but with weak defensibility in a crowded home services market.
notes: SeedTable lists a January 2014 round led by Sam Altman, seen in one aggregator only so left as unverified, not recorded. Sources conflict on the seed lead (SeedTable says Ram Shriram, TechCrunch says Sam Altman); TechCrunch used. The 2012 funding and launch articles name no competitors, so the competitor list comes from a 2011 CNN Money piece on errand services. Purchase price under 10 million is from a TechCrunch headline only.
